stories.title: BlackRock's Proposed Bitcoin ETF Would Hold No Bitcoin
stories.summary: BlackRock filed for a new Bitcoin-linked ETF. The filing states the fund would not hold Bitcoin itself, nor shares of spot Bitcoin ETFs. The report did not specify what the fund would hold instead.
stories.whyItMatters: A Bitcoin ETF that holds no Bitcoin raises basic questions about the exposure investors would actually buy.
whatToWatch: Any clarification from BlackRock on the fund's real holdings
questions: What assets would the fund hold instead of Bitcoin?
How would it track Bitcoin's price without holding it?

sources.title: BlackRock’s proposed Bitcoin ETF would hold no Bitcoin or spot ETF shares

stories.title: Bitcoin ETF Rebound Opens $630 Million Gap With Ethereum Funds
stories.summary: Bitcoin ETFs posted a rebound in inflows. Ethereum ETFs lagged far behind, leaving a reported $630 million gap between the two. BlackRock's funds took most of the Bitcoin-side inflows.
stories.whyItMatters: The flow gap shows institutions currently favor Bitcoin exposure over Ethereum, and shows how concentrated that demand is in one issuer.
whatToWatch: Continued concentration of inflows in BlackRock's funds
questions: What is driving the preference for Bitcoin over Ethereum right now?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETF comeback exposes a $630 million divide with Ethereum as BlackRock dominates

stories.title: Bullish Bitcoin Bets Could Worsen the Next Selloff
stories.summary: An analysis warns that traders still holding bullish Bitcoin positions could amplify a future price drop. Forced unwinding of those bets could add extra selling pressure if prices fall. The report frames this as a risk in current positioning, not a forecast of an imminent crash.
stories.whyItMatters: Crowded bullish positioning is a known setup for sharper downside moves, so readers sizing crypto risk should note it.
whatToWatch: Shifts in futures and options positioning data
Any sharp price move that tests these positions
questions: How concentrated is this bullish positioning, and among which traders?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s next selloff could be amplified by the traders still betting on its recovery

stories.title: NGRAVE Wallet Users Hit by $2.65 Million Phishing Attack
stories.summary: Attackers targeted users of the NGRAVE hardware wallet in a phishing campaign. The reported losses total $2.65 million. CryptoSlate frames the incident as part of a wider pattern of attacks on crypto wallet users.
stories.whyItMatters: Phishing attacks that reach hardware wallet users undercut the core security promise of self-custody.
whatToWatch: NGRAVE's response and any security guidance or patches
questions: How did attackers reach these users: fake sites, compromised software, or social engineering?

sources.title: Crypto wallet security crisis deepens as NGRAVE users face $2.65 million phishing attack

stories.title: Super League Shareholders Approve Metaplanet's 2,100 BTC Investment
stories.summary: Shareholders of Super League approved a plan tied to a 2,100 BTC investment involving Metaplanet. No further structural details were given in the report.
stories.whyItMatters: It is another sign of corporate treasuries adding Bitcoin, a trend readers tracking institutional adoption should track.
questions: What does this investment give each company: a stake, a partnership, or something else?

sources.title: Super League shareholders approve Metaplanet’s 2,100 BTC investment

stories.title: JPMorgan Launches JPM Coin on Ethereum for Institutions Only
stories.summary: JPMorgan deployed its JPM Coin on the Ethereum network. Access is limited to institutional clients, with no retail availability.
stories.whyItMatters: A major bank issuing a token on a public blockchain, even in gated form, signals growing Wall Street use of Ethereum infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Whether JPMorgan expands JPM Coin to other chains or to retail
questions: Why did JPMorgan choose Ethereum specifically?

sources.title: JPMorgan drops JPM Coin on Ethereum with zero retail access

stories.title: Bitcoin Fell 1.3% While Nasdaq-100 Dropped 5.5% in Last Week's Tech Selloff
stories.summary: During last week's tech stock selloff, Bitcoin fell 1.3%. The Nasdaq-100 lost 5.5% over the same period, a much steeper decline.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's smaller drop during this selloff is one data point on its behavior during broader risk-off moves in markets.
whatToWatch: Whether this divergence holds in future risk-off periods
questions: Does this reflect a real shift in Bitcoin's correlation with tech stocks, or a one-off?

sources.title: Bitcoin fell 1.3% while Nasdaq-100 lost 5.5% in last week’s tech selloff

stories.title: French Lawmakers Back Crypto Tax That Covers Stablecoin Swaps
stories.summary: Members of the French parliament backed a crypto tax measure. The measure extends to stablecoin swaps, not just cash-outs to fiat currency.
stories.whyItMatters: Taxing stablecoin swaps would raise the cost of routine crypto trading for users in France.
whatToWatch: Whether the measure passes into law
Reaction from French exchanges and crypto users
questions: What tax rate would apply, and does it cover every swap or only certain transactions?

sources.title: French MPs back crypto tax, and stablecoin swaps take the hit

stories.title: Bot Wallets Drive Most RLUSD Payment Activity on XRP Ledger
stories.summary: A report found that 110 bot wallets account for a large share of RLUSD stablecoin payments on the XRP Ledger. This raises questions about how much of the network's reported payment growth is organic.
stories.whyItMatters: If automated wallets drive most reported activity, that complicates claims about genuine adoption of XRP Ledger payments.
whatToWatch: Any response from Ripple or the XRP Ledger Foundation
Further breakdowns of RLUSD transaction data
questions: Who operates these bot wallets, and what purpose do they serve?

sources.title: XRP Ledger’s booming activity faces scrutiny as 110 bot wallets dominate RLUSD payments

stories.title: BNB Chain Splits Asset Control Into Four Roles, but Admins Keep the Key
stories.summary: BNB Chain restructured control over assets into four separate roles. Administrators still hold ultimate key control despite the split.
stories.whyItMatters: Splitting roles can look like decentralization, but a retained admin key means centralized trust assumptions remain for users.
whatToWatch: Any further decentralization steps from BNB Chain
Independent audits confirming how the power split works in practice
questions: What checks, if any, limit what the admin role can do?

sources.title: BNB Chain splits asset power across 4 roles while admins hold the key
